thread.title: Attorney General charges Fay Beydoun with 16 felonies for alleged misuse of grant funds
thread.title_full: Attorney General charges Fay Beydoun with 16 felonies for alleged misuse of grant funds

author: a. u. ward
title: Attorney General charges Fay Beydoun with 16 felonies for alleged misuse of grant funds
text:
Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel announced on May 6 that Fay Beydoun, a resident of Farmington Hills, faces 16 felony charges for allegedly stealing and misusing funds from a $20 million state legislative grant awarded to Global Link International, a company she created and controlled. The charges stem from accusations that Beydoun used the appropriated money for personal expenses and enrichment while providing false information about business activities to the Michigan Economic Development Corporation.
The case highlights concerns over the oversight and administration of public funding. According to Nessel, “Today, we allege Fay Beydoun sought and received a $20 million ‘Michigan enhancement grant’ from the state Legislature, operated a criminal enterprise to use those funds for personal expenses and her own enrichment, and lied repeatedly when reporting how she used those funds.” Nessel also said that the process by which this grant was handled did not resemble traditional procedures and was enabled by political cronyism paired with minimal oversight.
Beydoun has been charged in the 47th District Court in Farmington Hills. The investigation into Global Link International’s funding remains ongoing. The specific charges include one count of conducting a criminal enterprise (a felony punishable by up to 20 years), seven counts of uttering and publishing (14-year felonies), one count of forgery (14-year felony), one count of larceny by conversion over $20,000 (10-year felony), and six counts of larceny by conversion between $1,000-$20,000 (5-year felonies).
The Attorney General’s office alleges that no businesses relocated to Michigan as intended through Global Link International’s efforts. Instead, it is claimed Beydoun used state money for her own benefit—including maintaining an annual salary of $550,000—and submitted fraudulent documentation regarding legal expenses, leases, event costs, home furnishings purchases totaling thousands of dollars each time as well as misleading reports to avoid termination of funding.
Nessel said some reforms have been enacted since the creation of this grant: “These reforms are meaningful, but with millions of dollars in public funding at hand, the State and each of its agencies must do more to prevent abuses… regardless of whether their recipients enjoy positions of power…” The Department opened its investigation in 2024; following reports in March 2025 about financial irregularities MEDC terminated Global Link’s state grant. In September 2025 more than $6.3 million held in accounts connected to Beydoun were frozen.
An arraignment date has not yet been set. The Attorney General’s office reminds the public that all criminal charges are allegations only; defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty.
